Heard on I.A. No.01/2023, which is an application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to
the appellant.

The appellant has been convicted and sentenced by the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 03-03-2023 passed in Session Trial No.65/2021 by the learned Additional Sessions Judge (F.T.C.) Jashpur, District Jashpur (C.G.) in the following manner with a direction to run all the jail sentences concurrently :-
 Conviction Sentence  U/s 343 of the IPC Rigorous Imprisonment for 1 year and fine of Rs.1,000/-, in default of payment of fine further R.I. for 3 months U/s 506-II of the Rigorous Imprisonment for 2 years and fine IPC of Rs.1,000/-, in default of payment of fine further R.I. for 3 months U/s 25 of Arms Act Rigorous Imprisonment for 3 years and fine of Rs.1,000/-, in default of payment of fine further R.I. for 3 months U/s 376(2)(n) of Rigorous Imprisonment for 10 years and fine Indian Penal Code of Rs.1,000/-, in default of payment of fine further R.I. for 3 months

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant would submit that the prosecutrix a fully grown-up lady and was a consenting party in making physical relation with the appellant who herself had gone to the house of the appellant and voluntarily engaged in making physical relation with him.
She stayed for about 3 days in the house of the appellant and has not made any complaint to anyone about the incident.
No injuries have been found on the body of the prosecutrix.

He would further submit that from the evidence of PW-1, the prosecutrix, it appears that she was having relationship with the appellant Ramprasad vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163497880/
1
since three years and in view of the evidence of the prosecutrix, no offence is prima facie made out against the appellant, yet he has been convicted.
He is in jail since 20-03-2021 and final adjudication of the appeal will take its own time.
Therefore, the appellant may be enlarged on bail.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposes the application.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the trial Court.

Considering the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties and further considering the evidence of the prosecutrix (PW-1) as well as her age and nature of the evidence led by the prosecution, I am inclined to release the appellants on bail.
Accordingly, I.A. No.01/2023, application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail is allowed.

It is directed that the jail sentence imposed upon the appellant shall remain suspended during the pendency of this appeal and he shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- with one surety in like sum to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the Registry of this Court on 28th of November, 2024.

He shall thereafter appear before the trial Court on a date to be given by the Registry of this Court and shall continue to appear there on all such subsequent dates as are given to him by the said Court, till disposal of this appeal.
List this case for final hearing in due course.
